metadata.title: 01 - Writing Systems: From Marks to Alphabet
01 - Writing Systems: From Marks to Alphabet

sections.text: Writing is not a natural human capability — it is a technology, invented independently perhaps three or four times in human history and diffused from those origins. Every modern western alphabet traces a single lineage through the Phoenician consonantal abjad. Understanding that lineage gives you the substrate on which all typography operates.

3200 BCE  SUMERIAN CUNEIFORM ─────────────────────────────────────────┐
          wedge marks in clay; syllabary + logograms                   │
          Logistics → eventually literature                            │
                                                                        │
3000 BCE  EGYPTIAN HIEROGLYPHICS ─────────────────────────────────────┤
          logographic + phonetic + determinative                        │
          Stone → Papyrus → Demotic (cursive abstraction)              │ Independent
                                                                        │ origins
1200 BCE  ORACLE BONE SCRIPT (China) ──────────────────────────────────┤
          logographic; ancestor of modern Chinese characters           │
          Evolved continuously; never alphabetized                     │
                                                                        │
1850 BCE  PROTO-SINAITIC (Sinai, Egypt) ───────────────────────────────┘
          Egyptian-influenced; Semitic mine workers
               │
               ▼
          WEST SEMITIC ABJAD
               │
1050 BCE  PHOENICIAN ─────── 22 consonants, no vowels, right-to-left
          trade alphabet; maximum portability
               │                     │
               ▼                     ▼
          800 BCE GREEK           ARAMAIC ─── Hebrew (square script)
          added vowels;                │
          left-to-right               └──── ARABIC (~400 CE standard)
          standardized
               │
          ETRUSCAN (~700 BCE; western Greek variant)
               │
          700 BCE LATIN ALPHABET
               │
               ├── Roman Monumental Capitals (stone-cut UPPERCASE)
               ├── Uncial (400–800 CE; rounded; vellum-optimized)
               ├── Half-Uncial (first true ascenders/descenders)
               ├── Carolingian Minuscule (789 CE; our LOWERCASE)
               └── Humanist Minuscule (1400s; Renaissance revival)
